neet_che_u15_t08_1.working: Only a terminal alkyne has an acidic sp C–H. Propyne (CH3C≡CH) reacts: CH3C≡CH + NaNH2 → CH3C≡CNa + NH3. Ethene, ethane and but-2-yne have no acidic hydrogen.

neet_che_u15_t08_2.working: Markovnikov hydration of propyne gives an enol, CH3C(OH)=CH2. This tautomerises to the ketone CH3COCH3, propanone.

neet_che_u15_t08_3.working: Birch-type reduction with Na in liquid NH3 is an anti addition of hydrogen. It converts an internal alkyne to the trans-alkene, giving trans-but-2-ene.

neet_che_u15_t08_4.working: Alkynes are less reactive than alkenes towards electrophilic addition, so A is false. The vinylic cation is less stable than an alkyl carbocation, so R is true.

neet_che_u15_t08_5.working: But-2-yne is an internal alkyne with no acidic hydrogen. It does not react with Na or with ammoniacal AgNO3, so I is false. Propyne adds 2 HBr by Markovnikov's rule to give CH3CBr2CH3, a gem-dihalide, so II is true.
